lemmas.proof_markdown: This is the sole assumed statement. The inequality $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D$ is formal rank deficiency, not merely failure of surjectivity. The containments $E\subseteq E_{\mathrm{acc}}$ and $R\subseteq T$ are part of the assumption, every $\ell_L$ is an affine bijection, and the cardinality in the reach condition counts distinct incident points.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Fix $0<\theta\le 1/4$. Let $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge 1$ and $0<a_\theta,c_\theta\le 1$ satisfy

$$
C_\theta\ge \frac{8K_\theta}{a_\theta}.
$$

Assume $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$: for every prime $p$, every integer $d$ satisfying $100<d<p$, every function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, every family of affine bijections

$$
\bigl(\ell_L:\mathbb{F}_p\to L\bigr)_{L\in\mathcal{L}},
$$

indexed by the affine lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_p^2$, and every family $(P_L)_{L\in\mathcal{L}}$ with $P_L\in\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ and $\deg P_L\le d$, define

$$
E_{\mathrm{acc}}
=
\left\{(\ell_L(t),L):L\in\mathcal{L},\ t\in\mathbb{F}_p,\ P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\right\},
$$

$$
\varepsilon=\frac{|E_{\mathrm{acc}}|}{p^2(p+1)},
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)
=
\max_{\substack{Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]\\ \deg_{\mathrm{tot}}Q\le d}}
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)].
$$

If

$$
\varepsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)^{1-\theta},
$$

then either

$$
\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\theta\varepsilon,
$$

or there exist an accepted bipartite graph $G=(X,T,E)$, a set $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $D$ such that

$$
X\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^2,
\qquad
T\subseteq\mathcal{L},
\qquad
E\subseteq E_{\mathrm{acc}}\cap(X\times T),
$$

$$
e(G):=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}\ge a_\theta\varepsilon,
\qquad
d\le D\le K_\theta d,
\qquad
|R|>D,
$$

and, upon defining

$$
V_D=
\left\{A\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]:
\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\right\}
$$

and

$$
\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\longrightarrow
\prod_{M\in R}\mathbb{F}_p[t]_{\le D},
\qquad
\Phi_{R,D}(A)=
\bigl(A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R},
$$

one has

$$
\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D.
$$

Moreover, every $L\in T$ satisfies

$$
\left|
\left\{x\in X:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\}\text{ with }(x,M)\in E\right\}
\right|>D.
$$
lemmas.title: Rank-or-Decode Hypothesis

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Put $\rho=d/p$ and $x=D/p$. From the threshold in P1 and the bound $D\le K_\theta d$,

$$
x
\le K_\theta\rho
\le \frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\varepsilon\rho^\theta
\le \frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{8}
\le \frac18.
$$

Thus $D<p$. Moreover,

$$
x^2+3x
\le \frac{25x}{8}
\le \frac{25a_\theta\varepsilon}{64}
<\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2}.
$$

The last inequality is the required cleanup-and-peeling budget.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1, suppose the structured alternative occurs. Then

$$
D<p,
\qquad
\frac{D}{p}\le\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{8}\le\frac18,
$$

and

$$
\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)^2+3\frac{D}{p}
<\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2}.
$$
lemmas.title: Characteristic Budget

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Rank deficiency supplies a nonzero polynomial $A_0\in\ker\Phi_{R,D}$. Replace $A_0$ by its squarefree radical $A$. Every selected-line identity survives because $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ is an integral domain, and the weighted degree does not increase.

If $A$ were independent of $Z$, then every one of the more than $D$ distinct lines in $R$ would divide a nonzero polynomial in $\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $D$, which is impossible. Hence $A$ depends on $Z$. By P2, $\deg_ZA<p$, so $Z$-dependence implies $A_Z\not\equiv0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1 and P2, suppose the structured alternative occurs. Then there exists a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ such that

$$
\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D,
\qquad
A_Z\not\equiv0,
$$

and, for every $M\in R$,

$$
A(\ell_M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0
$$

as an identity in $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$.
lemmas.title: Squarefree Rank Kernel

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $L\in T$. For every reached point $x=\ell_L(t)=\ell_M(s)$ with $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$, acceptedness gives

$$
P_L(t)=f(x)=P_M(s).
$$

The selected-line identity on $M$ therefore yields

$$
A(x,P_L(t))=A(x,P_M(s))=0.
$$

There are more than $D$ distinct reached points on $L$, whereas the polynomial

$$
t\longmapsto A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))
$$

has degree at most $D$. Root counting forces this polynomial to vanish identically.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1 and P3, every $L\in T$ satisfies

$$
A(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0
$$

as an identity in $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$.
lemmas.title: Reached-Line Extension

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Squarefreeness of $A$ implies that $B$ is squarefree. Moreover,

$$
A_Z=HB_Z\not\equiv0,
$$

so $B$ depends on $Z$. If $L\notin T_{\mathrm{con}}$, the identity from P4 becomes

$$
H(\ell_L(t))B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.
$$

Since $H(\ell_L(t))$ is nonzero and $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ is an integral domain, cancellation gives

$$
B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.
$$

Each line in $T_{\mathrm{con}}$ supplies a distinct linear factor of $H$. Hence

$$
|T_{\mathrm{con}}|\le\deg H\le D.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P3 and P4, write

$$
A(X,Y,Z)=\sum_j a_j(X,Y)Z^j,
\qquad
H(X,Y)=\gcd_j a_j(X,Y),
\qquad
B=A/H.
$$

Then $H\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$, and $B\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ is primitive, squarefree, and $Z$-dependent, with

$$
\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B\le D,
\qquad
B_Z\not\equiv0.
$$

Define

$$
T_{\mathrm{con}}
=
\left\{L\in T:H(\ell_L(t))\equiv0\right\}.
$$

Then

$$
|T_{\mathrm{con}}|\le\deg H\le D,
$$

and every $L\in T\setminus T_{\mathrm{con}}$ satisfies

$$
B(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.
$$
lemmas.title: Primitive Relation

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Suppose an irreducible polynomial $C$ divides both $B$ and $B_Z$. Squarefreeness of $B$ forces $C_Z=0$. Since $\deg_ZC<p$, the polynomial $C$ is independent of $Z$, contradicting primitivity of $B$. Therefore

$$
\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.
$$

KTZ Lemma 2.6 bounds the number of lines on whose polynomial graphs both $B$ and $B_Z$ vanish identically by $D(D-1)$. Including the content lines from P5 gives fewer than $D^2$ bad lines.

On every other line, $B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most

$$
D-d\le D.
$$

It therefore has at most $D$ zeros. Deleting all incidences on bad lines and all remaining nonsimple incidences removes normalized mass less than

$$
\frac{D^2p}{p^2(p+1)}
+
\frac{Dp(p+1)}{p^2(p+1)}
<
\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)^2+ rac{D}{p}.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P2 and P5,

$$
\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.
$$

Define

$$
T_{\mathrm{ram}}
=
\left\{L\in T\setminus T_{\mathrm{con}}:
B_Z(\ell_L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0\right\}
$$

and

$$
E_0
=
\left\{(x,L)\in E:
L\notin T_{\mathrm{con}}\cup T_{\mathrm{ram}},\ B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0\right\}.
$$

Then

$$
|T_{\mathrm{con}}\cup T_{\mathrm{ram}}|<D^2,
$$

 every $(x,L)\in E_0$ satisfies

$$
B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad
B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0,
$$

and

$$
\frac{|E\setminus E_0|}{p^2(p+1)}
<
\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)^2+ rac{D}{p}.
$$
lemmas.title: Vertical Cleanup

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Starting with the graph having edge set $E_0$, iteratively delete every current point or line vertex of degree at most $D$. Charge each edge when its first endpoint is deleted. Every edge is charged once, and there are at most $p^2$ point vertices and $p(p+1)$ line vertices. Hence the normalized peeling cost is less than

$$
\frac{D\bigl(p^2+p(p+1)\bigr)}{p^2(p+1)}
<\frac{2D}{p}.
$$

Together with P6, the total normalized loss is less than

$$
\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)^2+3\frac{D}{p}
<\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2},
$$

where the final inequality is P2. Since $e(G)\ge a_\theta\varepsilon$, the surviving graph has normalized edge mass at least $a_\theta\varepsilon/2$ and is nonempty. Every surviving vertex has degree greater than $D$, and the clean root conditions are inherited from $E_0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1, P2, and P6, iteratively delete from the graph with edge set $E_0$ every current point or line vertex of degree at most $D$. The resulting graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ is nonempty and satisfies

$$
e(G_1)=\frac{|E_1|}{p^2(p+1)}
\ge\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2},
\qquad
\delta(G_1)>D.
$$

Every $x\in X_1$ satisfies

$$
B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad
B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.
$$
lemmas.title: Peeled Clean Core

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix a connected component $\Gamma$ and a point vertex $b$ in it. More than $D$ distinct incident graph lines pass through the simple root $(b,f(b))$. The characteristic-free formal implicit recursion at this root, dividing only by

$$
B_Z(b,f(b))\ne0,
$$

gives a unique formal bivariate branch. Truncate it at total degree $d$ to obtain $Q_\Gamma$.

For every line $L$ incident to $b$, the truncation satisfies

$$
Q_\Gamma(\ell_L(t))\equiv P_L(t).
$$

Consequently, $B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))$ has total degree at most $D$ and vanishes identically on more than $D$ distinct lines. Hence

$$
B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0.
$$

Across any edge of $\Gamma$, the restrictions $Q_\Gamma(\ell_L(t))$ and $P_L(t)$ are formal roots with the same simple initial value. Formal uniqueness makes them identical. Induction along paths in $\Gamma$ therefore gives $Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of $\Gamma$. This is the mechanism of KTZ Lemmas 2.5, 2.7, 6.1, and 6.3.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P2 and P7, for every connected component $\Gamma$ of $G_1$ there exists a polynomial $Q_\Gamma\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0
$$

and

$$
Q_\Gamma(x)=f(x)
$$

for every point vertex $x$ of $\Gamma$.
lemmas.title: Component Polynomial

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Polynomial division in $\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y][Z]$ by the monic polynomial $Z-Q_\Gamma(X,Y)$ shows that

$$
B(X,Y,Q_\Gamma(X,Y))\equiv0
$$

is equivalent to

$$
Z-Q_\Gamma(X,Y)\mid B(X,Y,Z).
$$

Distinct polynomials $Q_\Gamma$ give distinct monic irreducible divisors. Their number is therefore at most $\deg_ZB$. Since $B$ has weighted degree at most $D$,

$$
\deg_ZB
\le\frac{\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B}{d}
\le\frac{D}{d}
\le K_\theta.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P5 and P8, the distinct component polynomials satisfy

$$
\left|
\left\{Q_\Gamma:\Gamma\in\operatorname{Comp}(G_1)\right\}
\right|
\le
\deg_ZB
\le
\frac{\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B}{d}
\le
\frac{D}{d}
\le K_\theta.
$$
lemmas.title: Component Templates

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Group the edges of $G_1$ according to their component polynomial. By P9 there are at most $K_\theta$ distinct templates, while P7 gives $e(G_1)\ge a_\theta\varepsilon/2$. Hence some template $Q$ is assigned an edge set $F\subseteq E_1$ satisfying

$$
\frac{|F|}{p^2(p+1)}
\ge\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2K_\theta}.
$$

By P8, $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point incident to an edge of $F$. Each point is incident to at most $p+1$ affine lines. If $S$ is the set of point endpoints of $F$, then

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]
\ge\frac{|S|}{p^2}
\ge\frac{|F|}{p^2(p+1)}
\ge\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2K_\theta}.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P7, P8, and P9, there exists a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]
\ge\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2K_\theta}.
$$
lemmas.title: Template Selection

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The direct alternative in $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ gives agreement at least $c_\theta\varepsilon$. In the structured alternative, P10 gives agreement at least

$$
\frac{a_\theta\varepsilon}{2K_\theta}.
$$

Taking the smaller of these two guarantees proves the conclusion.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ and the hypotheses and notation of P1, define

$$
c_\theta^*
=
\min\left\{c_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}.
$$

If

$$
\varepsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)^{1-\theta},
$$

then there exists a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]
\ge c_\theta^*\varepsilon.
$$
lemmas.title: Fixed-Parameter Decoder

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $\eta\in(0,1)$ and take

$$
\theta=\min\left\{\eta,\frac14\right\}.
$$

Put $\rho=d/p$. Since $0<\rho<1$ and $\theta\le\eta$,

$$
\rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.
$$

Choose $C_\eta=C_\theta$ and $c_\eta=c_\theta^*$. The assumed $\eta$-threshold then implies the $\theta$-threshold in P11, whose conclusion supplies the required polynomial.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Assume that, for every $\theta\in(0,1/4]$, there exist constants $C_\theta,K_\theta\ge1$ and $0<a_\theta,c_\theta\le1$ satisfying

$$
C_\theta\ge\frac{8K_\theta}{a_\theta},
$$

for which $\mathrm{RD}_\theta$ from P1 holds. Then, for every fixed $\eta\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that the following holds.

For every prime $p$, every integer $d$ satisfying $100<d<p$, every function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, every family of affine bijections $(\ell_L:\mathbb{F}_p\to L)_{L\in\mathcal{L}}$, and every family $(P_L)_{L\in\mathcal{L}}$ with $P_L\in\mathbb{F}_p[t]$ and $\deg P_L\le d$, define

$$
\varepsilon
=
\frac{
\left|
\left\{(\ell_L(t),L):L\in\mathcal{L},\ t\in\mathbb{F}_p,\ P_L(t)=f(\ell_L(t))\right\}
\right|
}{p^2(p+1)}.
$$

If

$$
\varepsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)^{1-\eta},
$$

then there exists a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]
\ge c_\eta\varepsilon.
$$
lemmas.title: Near-Linear Exponents
